# Zotero PDF batch mode

Discovery summaries are abstract-based. To summarize **full PDFs** already in
your Zotero library, use `--zotero-collection`.

## Finding your collection path

The path is the one shown in Zotero's collection tree, not the random
`~/Zotero/storage/...` folder name. For a library that looks like this in
Zotero's sidebar:

```text
My Library
├── Reading
│   ├── Deep Reading          →  --zotero-collection "Reading/Deep Reading"
│   └── Skimmed               →  --zotero-collection "Reading/Skimmed"
├── Writing
│   └── CHI 2027 submission   →  --zotero-collection "Writing/CHI 2027 submission"
└── Inbox                     →  --zotero-collection "Inbox"
```

Ask PaperTracker rather than transcribing by hand:

```bash
uv run papertracker --list-zotero-collections
```

If two collections share a leaf name, use the full path. An optional
`My Library/` prefix is accepted and ignored.

Zotero's data directory is `~/Zotero` by default on macOS, Linux, and Windows
alike. Point `PAPERTRACKER_ZOTERO_DIR` elsewhere if you moved it.

## Running it

```bash
uv run papertracker --list-zotero-collections
uv run papertracker --zotero-collection "Reading/Deep Reading"
uv run papertracker --zotero-collection "Reading/Deep Reading" --template deep-human-study
uv run papertracker --zotero-collection "Reading/Deep Reading" --select
uv run papertracker --zotero-collection "Reading/Deep Reading" --zotero-include-subcollections
```

For both Claude and Codex, PaperTracker extracts text locally, preserves page
labels, processes every extractable page in bounded chunks, recursively
consolidates notes when needed, and only then fills the selected template. A
missing or image-only PDF fails before an LLM call with an `OCR required`
message; partially extractable PDFs continue with a warning. Output lands in
`user_data/digests/<project-id>/zotero/<collection>/`.

Because these are full-text runs, use a `fulltext` template — see
[Summary templates](templates.md#writing-one).

## Your library is never modified

The Zotero database is opened **read-only**: PaperTracker copies
`zotero.sqlite` to a temporary file first, then opens that copy with SQLite's
`mode=ro`. Zotero holds a lock on the live database while it runs, and the copy
is what makes the read safe. Nothing is written back, and the temporary copy is
deleted when the run ends.
